name: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate

lead: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate is a chemically modified version of the peptide Semax, with changes meant to help it resist breakdown and last longer in the body. Users seek sharper focus and stamina than the parent peptide gives.

The chain is indirect: better focus and cognition, more productivity and consistency, steadier training and routine. It is presumed to act like Semax, which is described as affecting neurotrophin (BDNF, NGF) expression in animal studies. No studies of this exact compound are reported; the benefits are extrapolated from Semax research.

paras: It is sold by research-chemical suppliers for laboratory use. Intranasal use is the route typically described for Semax-type peptides, and no established timeline exists.
It is not approved for human use in most jurisdictions. Safety in people has not been studied.

angle.text: This acetylated, amidated Semax analogue is sold as a research chemical, with users seeking sharper focus and stamina that carry into steadier training and routines. Any link to looks runs through habit consistency. The analogue itself has no direct studies; the research relates to Semax.

lead: N-Acetyl Semax Amidate is a synthetic heptapeptide analog of Semax, sold by research-chemical suppliers as a longer-lasting, intranasally used nootropic. It has no direct effect on the face or body; people who take interest in it do so for focus, mood and mental drive, hoping these support consistent training, skincare and other self-improvement routines. [1][2]

Its sequence is Ac-Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro-NH2, a Semax backbone with an acetyl cap at the N-terminus and an amide at the C-terminus, changes described as intended to resist enzymatic breakdown. [1] Semax itself was developed in Russia from a fragment of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), first described in the scientific literature in 1991, and is a prescription drug there for conditions including stroke and cognitive disorders. [2]

The modified compound is supplied for laboratory use and is not approved for human therapeutic use. Claimed benefits are extrapolated from Semax research; no direct studies of this variant are reported. [1]
infobox: Semax, Russian ACTH(4-10) analog; prescription in Russia [2]

paras: Semax is described as having poor oral bioavailability and is given as a nasal spray or by injection; online vendors market it as a nootropic. [2] Reference text describes N-Acetyl Semax Amidate as primarily used intranasally in research settings. [1] On T Nation, forum members have mentioned Semax in nootropic and wellbeing discussions, including a thread asking whether it affects libido and a post suggesting it alongside methylene blue. [3][4]

The acetyl group at the N-terminus is described as blocking aminopeptidases, and the amide at the C-terminus as blocking carboxypeptidases. [1] The stability benefits are described as hypothesized and unverified for this specific compound. [1]
No studies found on N-Acetyl Semax Amidate itself. Findings on unmodified Semax come mainly from Russian clinical use and animal work. [1][2]

Animal studies of unmodified Semax report increased brain-derived neurotrophic factor and its receptor TrkB in the hippocampus, activation of serotonergic and dopaminergic systems, and antidepressant-like and anxiolytic-like effects; the exact mechanism is unknown, and it may interact with melanocortin receptors and inhibit enkephalin-degrading enzymes. [2] Whether the modified analog behaves the same way has not been tested. [1]

lore.intro: Semax-family peptides come up in forum nootropic and hormone threads on T Nation, usually as passing mentions. [3][4]

claims.claim: Semax is a useful nootropic add-on.

timeline.event: Semax first described in the scientific literature. [2]
